uncited: The core data structure is a neural network $E_\theta$ combined with an input encoding scheme.
*   **Hash Table:** Stores latent vectors for finer levels.
Sample position-direction pairs $(x, n)$ throughout the scene volume.
Discard samples located inside scene geometry.
*   **Hash Collisions:** Many positions may map to the same latent vectors in the hash table.
These are implicitly handled during optimization as gradients from more important samples dominate the averaged gradient.
*   **Dark Leaks:** Samples inside geometry can waste capacity and cause dark leaks near static surfaces.
Neural Scene Volume Fields that use discrete coordinates and sparse volumes.
Unlike NIV, which learns a pre-integrated irradiance field for diffuse shading, NSVF models typically represent radiance or density directly.
Choose NSVF for general neural radiance field reconstruction; choose NIV for real-time diffuse global illumination of dynamic objects in static scenes. [11063-disco-nsvf-models.md]
*   **When to Use:** Real-time rendering of diffuse global illumination in scenes with static environments and dynamic objects, where memory and latency are constrained.
